title: Dependency Ownership Stripmap and Cross-Team Cutover Acceptance Protocol
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Cross-team roadmap cutovers regularly suffer from unclear ownership boundaries and inconsistent acceptance criteria, causing last-minute rollbacks or extended stabilization windows. Goal: Create a compact, actionable 'Stripmap' artifact that clearly assigns ownership bands (Primary, Escalation, Observability), defines deterministic acceptance gates per team (Eng, Design, Security, Infra), and gives PMs a single-pane readiness signal for go/no-go cutover decisions. Success criteria: (1) Reduce cutover rollbacks related to unclear ownership by 60% in the next two quarters; (2) All >=P1 roadmap cutovers must attach a Stripmap and a signed Cutover Acceptance badge prior to the production window; (3) PMs can make a go decision with a single glance at the readiness scorecard.
acceptance_criteria:
- Stripmap template published in Confluence with examples for feature, infra, and security cutovers.
- Cutover Acceptance badge (signed acknowledgement) integrated into Linear workflow and required for production deployment.
- Dashboard card in Console that aggregates per-team readiness signals and highlights missing artifacts.
- At least 3 pilot cutovers use the protocol and report post-mortem metrics.
approach: 1) Run 2-week discovery interviewing Eng, Design, Security, Infra PM/Leads to enumerate common failure modes; 2) Draft a lightweight Stripmap (one page) that maps components -> ownership band -> acceptance test; 3) Create a Cutover Acceptance checklist with explicit sign-off lines per team and a small JSON schema for automation; 4) Integrate badge into Linear (PR template + status) and surfaced in Console readiness card; 5) Pilot with two initiatives and iterate based on feedback.
deliverables: Linear automation: Cutover Acceptance badge + required checklist
Console card: Roadmap cutover readiness aggregation
Pilot runbook and postmortem for 3 pilots
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Teams treat Stripmap as bureaucratic checklist. Mitigation: Keep template < 1 page, automated reminders, and tie to deployment gates only for >=P1 cutovers. Risk: Security acceptance adds late blockers. Mitigation: Define 'early security signoff' and fast-track review lane in the Stripmap with a 48-hour SLA for high-priority cutovers.
notes: This ticket focuses on tooling + lightweight process, not on changing SLAs. We will coordinate with Infra on adding observability probes to the console card. Will propose a small policy that if a team cannot provide a signed acceptance within the window, we default to the Escalation owner and execute rollback automation.
